{{notability|date=October 2019}}

In [[applied mathematics]], the '''Morlely–Wang–Xu (MWX) element'''<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Wang |first1=Ming |last2=Xu |first2=Jinchao |title=Minimal finite element spaces for 2m-th-order partial differential equations in R^n |url=https://www.ams.org/journals/mcom/2013-82-281/S0025-5718-2012-02611-1/ |journal=Mathematics of Computation |volume=82 |issue=281 |pages=25–43 |doi=10.1090/S0025-5718-2012-02611-1|doi-access=free }}</ref> is a canonical construction of a family of piecewise polynomials with the minimal degree elements for any <math>2m</math>-th order of elliptic and parabolic equations in any spatial-dimension <math>\mathbb{R}^n</math> for <math>1\leq m \leq n</math>. The MWX element provides a consistent approximation of [[Sobolev space]] <math>H^m</math> in <math>\mathbb{R}^n</math>.

==Morley–Wang–Xu element==
The Morley–Wang–Xu element <math>(T,P_T,D_T)</math> is described as follows. <math>T</math> is a simplex and <math>P_T = P_m(T) </math>. The set of degrees of freedom will be given next.

Given an <math>n</math>-simplex <math>T</math> with vertices <math>a_i</math>, for <math>1\leq k\leq n</math>, let <math>\mathcal{F}_{T,k}</math> be the set consisting of all <math>(n-k)</math>-dimensional subsimplices of <math>T</math>. For any <math>F \in \mathcal{F}_{T,k}</math>, let <math>|F|</math> denote its measure, and let <math>\nu_{F,1}, \cdots, \nu_{F,k} </math> be its unit outer normals which are linearly independent.

For <math>1\leq k\leq m</math>, any <math>(n-k)</math>-dimensional
subsimplex <math>F\in \mathcal{F}_{T,k}</math> and <math>\beta\in A_k</math> with <math>|\beta|=m-k</math>, define

: <math>
d_{T,F,\beta}(v) = \frac{1}{|F|}\int_F \frac{\partial^{|\beta|}v}{\partial \nu_{F,1}^{\beta_1} \cdots \nu_{F,k}^{\beta_k}}.
</math>

The degrees of freedom are depicted in Table 1. For <math>m=n=1</math>, we obtain the well-known conforming linear element. For <math>m=1</math> and <math>n\geq 2</math>, we obtain the well-known nonconforming Crouziex–Raviart element. For   <math>m=2</math>, we recover the well-known Morley element for <math>n=2</math> and its generalization to <math>n\geq 2</math>. For <math>m=n=3</math>, we obtain a new cubic element on a simplex that has 20 degrees of freedom.
[[File:MWX Table.png|thumb|Table 1: m <= n+1: diagrams of the finite elements]]

==Generalizations==
There are two generalizations of Morley–Wang–Xu element (which requires <math>1\leq m \leq n</math>).

===<math>m=n+1</math>: Nonconforming element===
As a nontrivial generalization of Morley–Wang–Xu elements, Wu and [[Jinchao Xu|Xu]] propose a universal construction for the more difficult case in which <math>m=n+1</math>.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Wu |first1=Shuonan |last2=Xu |first2=Jinchao |title=Nonconforming finite element spaces for 2mth order partial differential equations on R^n simplicial grids when ''m''&nbsp;=&nbsp;''n''&nbsp;+&nbsp;1 |url=https://www.ams.org/journals/mcom/2019-88-316/S0025-5718-2018-03361-0/home.html |journal=Mathematics of Computation |date=2017 |volume=88 |issue=316 |pages=531–551 |doi=10.1090/mcom/3361|arxiv=1705.10873 }}</ref> Table 1 depicts the degrees of freedom for the case that <math>n\leq3, m\leq n+1</math>. The shape [[function space]] is <math>\mathcal{P}_{n+1}(T)+q_T\mathcal{P}_1(T)</math>, where <math>q_T = \lambda_1\lambda_2\cdots\lambda_n+1</math> is volume bubble function. This new family of finite element methods provides practical [[discretization]] methods for, say, a sixth order elliptic equations in 2D (which only has 12 local degrees of freedom). In addition, Wu and [[Jinchao Xu|Xu]] propose an <math>H^3</math> nonconforming finite element that is robust for the sixth order singularly perturbed problems in 2D.

===<math>m,n \geq 1</math>: Interior penalty nonconforming FEMs===
An alternative generalization when <math>m > n</math> is developed by combining the interior penalty and nonconforming methods by Wu and [[Jinchao Xu|Xu]]. This family of finite element space consists of piecewise polynomials of degree not greater than <math>m</math>. The degrees of freedom are carefully designed to preserve the weak-continuity as much as possible. For the case in which <math>m>n</math>, the corresponding interior penalty terms are applied to obtain the convergence property. As a simple example, the proposed method for the case in which <math>m = 3, n = 2</math> is to find <math>u_h\in V_h</math>, such that

: <math>
(\nabla^3_h u_h, \nabla^3_h v_h) + \eta \sum_{F\in \mathcal{F}_h} h_F^{-5}\int_F [u_h][v_h] = (f,v_h) \quad \forall v_h \in V_h,
</math>

where the nonconforming element is depicted in Figure 1. [[File:MWX Fig.png|thumb|Figure 1: m,n <= 1: The nonconforming element]].
